chunks: From him, from Safwan, from Abu Muhammad al-Khayyat, from Mujammir, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Do I accept garments, sew them, and then give them to the boys for two-thirds [of the value]?' He said: 'Do you not work on them?' I said: 'I cut them and buy the thread for them.' He said: 'There is no harm.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pay tailors by providing the fabric and thread while keeping a portion of the finished garments?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the mechanics of *Ijara* (contracting for work), specifically addressing whether a tailor can accept garments, pay workers two-thirds of the fee, and retain the remainder by supplying materials and performing the cutting. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates this arrangement, establishing that providing inputs and labor constitutes a valid share in the service contract, a principle foundational to Shia commercial jurisprudence regarding mixed labor-and-material contributions.
